title.zh: 卷四 本紀第四 少帝
title.raw: 卷四 本紀第四 少帝 Volume 4 Annals 4: Emperor Shao

sentences.zh: 永初三年五月癸亥，武帝崩，是日，太子即皇帝位。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu, in the fifth month, on the day guihai, Emperor Wu died; that same day, the crown prince took the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Yongchu, on the day guihai, Emperor Wu died. That same day the crown prince ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 尊皇太后曰太皇太后。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was elevated to grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 六月壬申，以尚書僕射傅亮為中書監，司空徐羨之、領軍將軍謝晦及亮輔政。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day renshen, Fu Liang, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Supervisor of the Central Secretariat; the Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi, the General Who Leads the Army Xie Hui, and Liang were made regents.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day renshen, Fu Liang, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed Supervisor of the Central Secretariat. Xu Xianzhi as Minister of Works, Xie Hui as General Who Leads the Army, and Liang were made regents.

sentences.zh: 戊子，太尉長沙王道憐薨。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, the Grand Marshal, Prince of Changsha, Dao Lin, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuzi, Grand Marshal Dao Lin, Prince of Changsha, died.

sentences.zh: 秋九月丁未，有司奏武皇帝配南郊，武敬皇后配北郊。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on the day dingwei, the relevant offices memorialized that Emperor Wu should be paired at the southern suburban altar and Empress Wu Jing at the northern suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, on the day dingwei, the relevant offices proposed that Emperor Wu be enshrined at the southern suburban altar and Empress Wu Jing at the northern suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月戊午，有星孛于營室。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day wuwu, a broom star appeared in Encampment.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day wuwu, a comet appeared in the Encampment mansion.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚戌，魏軍克滑臺。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day gengxu, Wei forces captured Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day gengxu, Wei troops captured Huatai.

sentences.zh: 明年春正月己亥朔，大赦，改元為景平元年。

translations.literal: In the spring of the following year, on the first day of the first month, the day jihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and the era name was changed to Jingping, year one.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the following year, on new year's day of the first month, the day jihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Jingping, year one.

sentences.zh: 文武進位二等。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials were advanced two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials were promoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，祀南郊。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, the southern suburb was sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinchou, sacrifices were offered at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: [3]虜將達奚卬破金墉，進圍虎牢。

translations.literal: [3] The barbarian general Daxi Ang captured Jinyong and advanced to besiege Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: [3] An enemy general, Daxi Ang, took Jinyong and advanced to besiege Hulao.

sentences.zh: [4]毛德祖擊虜敗之，虜退而復合。

translations.literal: [4] Mao Dezu attacked the barbarians and defeated them; the barbarians withdrew and then regathered.
translations.idiomatic: [4] Mao Dezu attacked the enemy and defeated them, but they withdrew only to regroup.

sentences.zh: 拓跋木末又遣安平公涉歸寇青州。

translations.literal: Tuoba Mumo again sent the Anping Duke Shegui to raid Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Mumo again sent the Duke of Anping, Shegui, to raid Qing Province.

sentences.zh: [5]癸卯，河南郡失守。

translations.literal: [5] On the day guimao, Henan Commandery was lost.
translations.idiomatic: [5] On the day guimao, Henan Commandery fell.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，有星孛于東壁。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, a broom star appeared in Eastern Wall.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimao, a comet appeared in the Eastern Wall mansion.

sentences.zh: 二月丁丑，太皇太后崩。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day dingchou, the grand empress dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day dingchou, the grand empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜、吐谷渾阿犲並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun and Tuyuhun Abao both sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun and Tuyuhun Abao both sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，[6]爵蒙遜為驃騎大將軍，[7]封河西王。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, [6] Mengxun was ennobled as Grand General of Agile Cavalry, [7] and enfeoffed as Prince of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengchen, [6] Mengxun was ennobled Grand General of Agile Cavalry [7] and created Prince of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 以阿犲為安西將軍、沙州刺史，封澆河公。

translations.literal: Abao was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Shazhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Jiaohe.
translations.idiomatic: Abao was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Sha Province, and enfeoffed as Duke of Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 辛未，富陽人孫法光反，[8]寇山陰，會稽太守褚淡之遣山陰令陸劭討敗之。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Sun Faguang of Fuyang rebelled, [8] raided Shanyin; Chuji Commandery Administrator Chu Danzhi sent Shanyin Magistrate Lu Shao to attack and defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei, Sun Faguang of Fuyang rebelled [8] and raided Shanyin. Chu Danzhi, administrator of Kuaiji Commandery, sent Shanyin magistrate Lu Shao, who defeated him.

translations.literal: Editorial note nine stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note nine stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.

sentences.zh: 三月壬寅，孝懿皇后祔葬于興寧陵。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day renyin, Empress Xiaoyi was escorted for joint burial at Xingning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day renyin, Empress Xiaoyi was buried alongside her consort at Xingning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 是月，高麗國遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That month, Goguryeo sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That same month, Goguryeo sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 甲子，豫州刺史劉粹遣軍襲許昌，殺虜潁川太守庾龍。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Liu Cui, Inspector of Yu Province, sent troops to raid Xuchang and killed the barbarian Administrator of Yingchuan, Yu Long.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi, Liu Cui, inspector of Yu Province, sent troops to strike Xuchang and killed the enemy administrator of Yingchuan, Yu Long.

sentences.zh: [10]乙丑，虜騎寇高平。

translations.literal: [10] On the day yichou, barbarian horsemen raided Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: [10] On the day yichou, enemy horsemen raided Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 初虜自河北之敗，請修和親；

translations.literal: At first, after their defeat in Hebei, the barbarians requested to restore friendly relations;
translations.idiomatic: After their defeat in Hebei, the northerners had sought to restore peaceful relations;

sentences.zh: 及聞高祖崩，因復侵擾，河、洛之地騷然矣。

translations.literal: when they heard that Gaozu had died, they again invaded and harassed, and the lands of the Yellow and Luo rivers were thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: but when they learned that Gaozu had died, they resumed their raids, and the Yellow and Luo regions were thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，檀道濟北征，次臨朐，焚虜攻具。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Tan Daoji marched north, halted at Linqu, and burned the barbarians' siege equipment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Tan Daoji marched north, camped at Linqu, and burned the enemy siege equipment.

sentences.zh: 乙未，魏軍克虎牢，執司州刺史毛德祖以歸。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Wei forces captured Hulao and took Mao Dezu, Inspector of Si Province, back with them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiwei, Wei troops took Hulao and carried off Mao Dezu, inspector of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸酉，尊所生張夫人為皇太后。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day guiyou, his birth mother, Lady Zhang, was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day guiyou, the emperor's birth mother, Lady Zhang, was elevated empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以旱，詔赦五歲刑以下罪人。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, because of drought, an edict pardoned offenders punished with penalties below five years.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou, owing to drought, an edict pardoned those sentenced to less than five years' punishment.

translations.literal: Editorial note eleven stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note eleven stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己未，有星孛于氐，指尾，貫攝提，向大角，仲月在危，季月掃天倉而後滅。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiwei, a broom star appeared in Room, pointing to Tail, piercing Monarch-Subduer, heading toward Great Horn; in the intercalary month it was in Rooftop, and in the last month it swept Celestial Granary and then vanished.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiwei, a comet appeared in Room, pointing toward Tail, running through Monarch-Subduer toward Great Horn; in the intercalary month it stood in Rooftop, and in the twelfth month it swept across Celestial Granary before vanishing.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏主拓跋嗣薨，子燾立。

translations.literal: That year, the Wei ruler Tuoba Si died, and his son Tao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the Wei ruler Tuoba Si died and was succeeded by his son Tao.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙寅，[12]省寧州之江陽、犍為、安上三郡，合為宋昌郡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day bingyin, [12] the three commanderies of Jiangyang, Qianwei, and Anshang in Ning Province were reduced and combined into Songchang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day bingyin, [12] the three commanderies of Jiangyang, Qianwei, and Anshang in Ning Province were abolished and combined into Songchang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 二年春二月癸巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, on the first day of the second month, the day guisi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year, on new year's day of the second month, the day guisi, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: [13]廢南豫州刺史廬陵王義真為庶人，徙新安郡。

translations.literal: [13] The Prince of Luling, Yizhen, was deposed as Inspector of South Yu Province to a commoner and moved to Xin'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: [13] Prince of Luling Yizhen, inspector of South Yu Province, was deposed to commoner status and exiled to Xin'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以皇弟義恭為冠軍將軍，南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, the emperor's younger brother Yigong was made General Who Vanquishes the Enemy and Inspector of South Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiwei, the emperor's younger brother Yigong was appointed General Who Vanquishes the Enemy and inspector of South Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，大風，[14]天有五色雲，占者以為有兵。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, a great wind blew; [14] five-colored clouds appeared in the sky, and diviners took it as a sign of war.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi, a violent wind rose; [14] five-colored clouds filled the sky, which diviners read as foretelling war.

sentences.zh: 高麗國遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: Goguryeo sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 執政使使者誅義真于新安。

translations.literal: The regents sent an envoy who put Yizhen to death at Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: The regents sent an envoy who put Yizhen to death at Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，江州刺史王弘、南兗州刺史檀道濟入朝。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer, Wang Hong, Inspector of Jiang Province, and Tan Daoji, Inspector of South Yan Province, entered the capital for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, Wang Hong, inspector of Jiang Province, and Tan Daoji, inspector of South Yan Province, came to court.

sentences.zh: [15]帝居處所為多過失。

translations.literal: [15] The emperor's conduct in daily life was full of many faults.
translations.idiomatic: [15] The emperor's conduct in daily life was full of grave faults.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，皇太后令曰：

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, the empress dowager issued an order saying:
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiyou, the empress dowager issued an order saying:

sentences.zh: 王室不造，天禍未悔，先帝創業弗永，棄世登遐。

translations.literal: The royal house has met misfortune; heaven's calamity has not yet relented. The late emperor's founding of the enterprise did not last long; he abandoned the world and ascended far away.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house has met with misfortune, and heaven's wrath has not yet relented. The late emperor's founding of the realm did not last long before he left the world and passed away.

sentences.zh: 義符長嗣，屬當天位，不謂窮凶極悖，一至於此。

translations.literal: Yifu, the eldest heir, ought to have inherited heaven's throne; who would have thought his wickedness and extreme perversity could reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu, as eldest heir, was meant to inherit the throne; who could have imagined that his wickedness and perversity would reach such an extreme.

sentences.zh: 大行在殯，宇內哀惶，幸災肆於悖詞，喜容表於在慼。

translations.literal: While the late emperor lay in coffin and all within the four seas mourned in fear, he exulted in disaster with perverse words and showed joy while supposedly in grief.
translations.idiomatic: While the late emperor still lay in state and the realm mourned in anguish, he exulted in misfortune with perverse words and showed a joyful face even amid supposed grief.

sentences.zh: 至乃徵召樂府，鳩集伶官，優倡管絃，靡不備奏，珍羞甘膳，有加平日。

translations.literal: He even summoned the Music Office, gathered players, had actors and string music all performed without exception, and delicacies and sweet dishes exceeded ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: He even summoned the Music Office, gathered players, and had actors and string ensembles perform without stint, while delicacies and sweet dishes surpassed those of ordinary days.

sentences.zh: 採擇媵御，產子就宮，靦然無怍，醜聲四達。

translations.literal: He selected concubines, brought them to the palace when they bore children, utterly without shame, and scandal spread in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: He selected concubines and brought them into the palace when they bore children, utterly without shame, until scandal spread in every direction.

sentences.zh: 及懿后崩背，重加天罰，親與左右執紼歌呼，推排梓宮，抃掌笑謔，殿省備聞。

translations.literal: When Empress Yi died, he doubled heaven's punishment, personally with attendants seized mourning cords and sang loudly, pushed the inner coffin, clapped hands and laughed, and all in the palace offices heard.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Yi died, he added fresh outrage to heaven's grief: he personally seized mourning cords with his attendants and sang aloud, pushed the inner coffin, clapped his hands and laughed—matters the palace offices all heard.

sentences.zh: 加復日夜媟狎，羣小慢戲，興造千計，費用萬端，帑藏空虛，人力殫盡。

translations.literal: Moreover by day and night he committed lewd intimacies, petty men indulged in coarse play, constructions numbered in thousands, expenses in myriads; the treasury was empty, human strength exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, by day and night he indulged in lewd intimacies while petty men engaged in coarse sport; constructions numbered in the thousands and expenses in the myriads, until the treasury stood empty and human strength was exhausted.

sentences.zh: 刑罰苛虐，幽囚日增。

translations.literal: Punishments were harsh and cruel, and prisoners in dungeons daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments grew harsh and cruel, and prisoners in the dungeons increased daily.

sentences.zh: 居帝王之位，好皁隸之役，處萬乘之尊，悅廝養之事。

translations.literal: Occupying an emperor's position, he delighted in black servants' labors; dwelling in ten-thousand-chariot eminence, he took pleasure in groom and stable chores.
translations.idiomatic: Though he occupied the throne of an emperor, he delighted in the labors of black-clad servants; though he held the dignity of ten thousand chariots, he took pleasure in groom and stable work.

sentences.zh: 親執鞭撲，毆擊無辜，以為笑樂。

translations.literal: He personally wielded whips, beat the innocent, and took it as laughter and fun.
translations.idiomatic: He personally wielded whips, beat the innocent, and made it his sport and amusement.

sentences.zh: 穿池築觀，朝成暮毀，徵發工匠，疲極兆民。

translations.literal: He dug ponds and built towers, finished in the morning and destroyed by evening, conscripted artisans, and exhausted the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: He dug ponds and built towers, finishing them in the morning and destroying them by evening, conscripted artisans, and wore out the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 遠近歎嗟，人神怨怒，社稷將墜，豈可復嗣守洪業，君臨萬邦。

translations.literal: Near and far lamented, men and spirits were enraged, the altars of state were about to fall—how could he again succeed to the great enterprise and preside over the myriad realms?
translations.idiomatic: Near and far lamented, men and spirits were enraged, and the altars of state were about to fall—how could he again succeed to the great enterprise and rule the myriad realms?

sentences.zh: 今廢為營陽王，一依漢昌邑、晉海西故事。

translations.literal: Now he is deposed as Prince of Yingyang, wholly following the precedents of Han's Marquis of Changyi and Jin's Prince of Haixi.
translations.idiomatic: He is now deposed as Prince of Yingyang, wholly following the precedents of Han's Marquis of Changyi and Jin's Prince of Haixi.

sentences.zh: 鎮〔西將軍宜都王，仁明孝弟，著自幼辰。

translations.literal: The General Who Guards the West, Prince of Yidu, is benevolent, bright, filial, and brotherly, manifest from early youth.
translations.idiomatic: The General Who Guards the West, Prince of Yidu, is benevolent, bright, filial, and brotherly—qualities evident from his earliest years.

sentences.zh: 德業沖粹，識心明允。

translations.literal: His virtue and achievement are pure, his mind knowing and clear.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue and conduct are pure, his understanding clear and his judgment sound.

sentences.zh: 宜纂洪統，光臨億兆。

translations.literal: He ought to succeed to the great succession and shed light upon the hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: He ought to succeed to the great succession and bring his radiance to the hundred millions.

sentences.zh: 主者詳依典故，以時奉迎。

translations.literal: Let the officials in charge examine the precedents in detail and install him in due season.
translations.idiomatic: Let the officials in charge examine the precedents in detail and install him at the proper time.

sentences.zh: 未亡人嬰此百罹，雖存若隕。

translations.literal: This surviving widow suffers these hundred calamities; though alive, she is as if fallen.
translations.idiomatic: This surviving widow is stricken with a hundred calamities; though alive, she is as one already fallen.

sentences.zh: 永悼情事，撫心摧塞。

translations.literal: Forever mourning these circumstances, she presses her heart and is crushed.
translations.idiomatic: Forever mourning these circumstances, she presses her heart and is utterly crushed.

translations.literal: Editorial note sixteen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note sixteen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.

sentences.zh: 始徐羨之、傅亮將廢帝，諷王弘、檀道濟求赴國訃。

translations.literal: At first, when Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang were about to depose the emperor, they hinted to Wang Hong and Tan Daoji to come for the state mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang were plotting to depose the emperor, they urged Wang Hong and Tan Daoji to come for the state mourning.

sentences.zh: 弘等來朝。

translations.literal: Hong and the others came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and the others came to court.

sentences.zh: 使中書舍人邢安泰、潘盛為內應。

translations.literal: They made Palace Attendants Xing Antai and Pan Sheng their inside contacts.
translations.idiomatic: They made Palace Attendants Xing Antai and Pan Sheng their agents within the palace.

sentences.zh: 是旦，道濟、謝晦領兵居前，羨之等隨後，因東掖門開，入自雲龍門。

translations.literal: That morning, Tan Daoji and Xie Hui led troops in front, while Xianzhi and the others followed; because the eastern side gate was opened, they entered through Cloud Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: That morning Tan Daoji and Xie Hui led troops in front while Xianzhi and the others followed; the eastern side gate was opened, and they entered through Cloud Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 盛等先戒宿衞，莫有禦者。

translations.literal: Sheng and the others had first warned the night guards, and none resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and the others had first warned the night guards, and none resisted.

sentences.zh: 時帝於華林園為列肆，親自酤賣。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was in Hualin Park setting up a row of shops and personally selling wine.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was in Hualin Park, where he had set up a row of shops and was personally selling wine.

sentences.zh: 又開瀆聚土，以象破岡埭，與左右引船唱呼，以為歡樂。

translations.literal: He also dug a channel and piled earth to imitate the Pogang dam, and with attendants pulled boats while shouting, taking it as pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He had also dug a channel and piled earth to imitate the Pogang dam, pulling boats with his attendants while shouting for joy.

sentences.zh: 夕游天淵池，即龍舟而寢。

translations.literal: In the evening he toured Heavenly Abyss Pool and slept on the dragon boat.
translations.idiomatic: In the evening he toured Heavenly Abyss Pool and slept aboard the dragon boat.

sentences.zh: 其朝未興，兵士進，殺二侍者於帝側，傷帝指。

translations.literal: Before dawn the soldiers entered, killed two attendants at the emperor's side, and wounded the emperor's finger.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn the soldiers entered, killed two attendants at the emperor's side, and wounded the emperor's finger.

sentences.zh: 夫出東閤，就收璽紱，羣臣拜辭，送於東宮，遂幽於吳郡。

translations.literal: He was taken out through the eastern wing, the seals and cords were collected, the officials bowed in farewell, he was sent to the eastern palace, and then confined in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was led out through the eastern wing; the seals and cords were taken, the officials bowed in farewell, and he was sent to the eastern palace before being confined in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 是日，赦死罪以下。

translations.literal: That day, those sentenced to death and below were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: That day, those sentenced to death or below were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 太后令奉還璽紱。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered that the seals and cords be returned.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered that the seals and cords be returned.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟入守朝堂。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji entered to guard the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji entered to guard the court hall.

sentences.zh: 六月癸丑，徐羨之等使中書舍人邢安泰弒帝於金昌亭。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day guichou, Xu Xianzhi and the others had Palace Attendant Xing Antai assassinate the emperor at Jinchang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day guichou, Xu Xianzhi and the others had Palace Attendant Xing Antai assassinate the emperor at Jinchang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 帝有勇力，不即受制，突走出昌門，追以門關踣之，致殞。

translations.literal: The emperor had courage and strength and did not immediately submit; he burst out through Chang Gate, and pursuers struck him down with the gate bar, causing his death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was strong and did not submit at once; he burst out through Chang Gate, but pursuers struck him down with the gate bar and killed him.

sentences.zh: 時年十九。

translations.literal: He was nineteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was nineteen years old.

translations.literal: Editorial note seventeen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note seventeen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.

sentences.zh: 〈上闕〉

translations.literal: The text above is missing.
translations.idiomatic: The text above is missing.

sentences.zh: 則創業之君，自天所啟；

translations.literal: Thus the ruler who founds the enterprise is opened by heaven itself;
translations.idiomatic: So the sovereign who founds the realm is heaven's own chosen;

sentences.zh: 守文之主，其難乎哉！

translations.literal: but one who merely keeps the written law—how hard it is!
translations.idiomatic: yet to merely keep the written legacy—how hard that is!

translations.literal: Editorial note eighteen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note eighteen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 武帝長子也 廿二史考異云：「按紀傳書諸帝皆稱廟號，獨此紀書武帝者四，而仍有稱高祖者。

translations.literal: He was Emperor Wu's eldest son. The Collected Variants in the Twenty-two Histories says: "According to the annals and biographies, all emperors are given their temple names; only this annal calls him Emperor Wu four times, and there are still places that call him Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: He was Emperor Wu's eldest son. The Collected Variants in the Twenty-two Histories says: "In the annals and biographies all emperors are given their temple names, yet this annal alone calls him Emperor Wu four times, and there are still passages that call him Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 又它篇例稱魏為索虜，而此紀一云魏軍克滑臺，一云魏主拓跋嗣薨，全非休文之例。

translations.literal: Again, other chapters by rule call Wei the 'barbarian Wei,' yet this annal once says 'Wei forces captured Huatai' and once 'the Wei ruler Tuoba Si died'—altogether unlike Shen Yue's usage.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere the book routinely calls Wei the 'barbarian Wei,' yet this annal once says 'Wei troops captured Huatai' and once 'the Wei ruler Tuoba Si died'—nothing like Shen Yue's usual practice.

sentences.zh: 又如義熙十二年正月，以豫章公世子為西中郎將、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Again, such as in the twelfth year of Yixi, in the first month, when the heir of the Duke of Yuzhang was made General of the West Center and Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: For example, in the twelfth year of Yixi, the first month, when the heir of the Duke of Yuzhang was made General of the West Center and inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 三月，除征虜將軍、徐兗二州刺史，鎮京口。

translations.literal: In the third month, he was relieved as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and made Inspector of Xu and Yan Provinces, stationed at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was relieved as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and made inspector of Xu and Yan provinces, stationed at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 十四年六月，除中軍將軍，副貳相國府。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year, he was relieved as General of the Center and made deputy to the Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year he was relieved as General of the Center and made deputy to the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 若宜見於本紀，而略不及。

translations.literal: If these ought to appear in this annal, they are altogether omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Events that ought to appear in this annal are altogether omitted.

sentences.zh: 卷末無史臣論。

translations.literal: At the end of the scroll there is no historian's appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the scroll there is no historian's appraisal.

sentences.zh: 其非休文書顯然。

translations.literal: That it is not Shen Yue's writing is obvious.
translations.idiomatic: That this is not Shen Yue's own writing is obvious.

sentences.zh: 蓋此篇久亡，後人雜採它書以補之，故義例乖舛如此。」

translations.literal: Presumably this chapter was long lost, and later men pieced it together from other books, hence such confused usage."
translations.idiomatic: Presumably the chapter was long lost and later men pieced it together from other books, hence such confused usage."

sentences.zh: 年十歲拜豫章公世子 按少帝義符生於義熙二年，而據五行志授豫章世子，在義熙七年，則當云六歲，此云十歲，疑有誤。

translations.literal: At age ten he was made heir of the Duke of Yuzhang. Commentary: Shaodi Yifu was born in the second year of Yixi, but according to the Treatise on the Five Phases the title of Yuzhang heir was granted in the seventh year of Yixi; it should say six years old—this says ten, which is suspected to be an error.
translations.idiomatic: At age ten he was made heir of the Duke of Yuzhang. Commentary: Emperor Shao Yifu was born in the second year of Yixi, but according to the Treatise on the Five Phases the title of Yuzhang heir was granted in the seventh year of Yixi; it should read six years old—here it says ten, which is suspected to be an error.

sentences.zh: 辛丑祀南郊 「辛丑」各本作「辛巳」，據局本及南史改。

translations.literal: On xinchou the southern suburb was sacrificed to: in all editions "xinchou" is written "xinsi"; changed according to the Bureau edition and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices at the southern suburb on xinchou: in all editions "xinchou" is written "xinsi"; changed according to the Bureau edition and the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 按是年正月己亥朔，無辛巳，初三日辛丑。

translations.literal: Commentary: In that year the first month began on jihai; there is no xinsi; on the third day was xinchou.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: That year new year's day of the first month was jihai; there is no xinsi; the third day was xinchou.

sentences.zh: 虜將達奚卬破金墉進圍虎牢 按據魏書奚斤傳，圍虎牢者為奚斤，斤本姓達奚氏。

translations.literal: The barbarian general Daxi Ang captured Jinyong and advanced to besiege Hulao. Commentary: According to the Wei History biography of Xi Jin, the besieger of Hulao was Xi Jin; Jin's original surname was the Daxi clan.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy general Daxi Ang took Jinyong and advanced to besiege Hulao. Commentary: According to the Wei History biography of Xi Jin, the besieger of Hulao was Xi Jin, whose clan name was originally Daxi.

sentences.zh: 「卬」當是「斤」字之譌。

translations.literal: "Ang" should be a corruption of the character "Jin."
translations.idiomatic: "Ang" is presumably a corruption of the character "Jin."

sentences.zh: 拓跋木末又遣安平公涉歸寇青州 拓跋木末即魏主拓跋嗣。

translations.literal: Tuoba Mumo again sent the Anping Duke Shegui to raid Qing Province. Commentary: Tuoba Mumo is the Wei ruler Tuoba Si.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Mumo again sent the Duke of Anping, Shegui, to raid Qing Province. Commentary: Tuoba Mumo is the Wei ruler Tuoba Si.

sentences.zh: 本卷後又稱嗣。

translations.literal: Later in this scroll he is again called Si.
translations.idiomatic: Later in this scroll he is again called Si.

sentences.zh: 蓋所採雜異，故前後不一致。

translations.literal: Presumably because the sources gathered were mixed and diverse, the text is inconsistent before and after.
translations.idiomatic: The sources used were evidently mixed, which explains the inconsistency.

sentences.zh: 「安平公」各本作「平安公」，今從局本。

translations.literal: "Anping Duke": in all editions it is written "Ping'an Duke"; now following the Bureau edition.
translations.idiomatic: "Duke of Anping": all editions read "Duke of Ping'an"; the text now follows the Bureau edition.

sentences.zh: 按索虜傳：「景平元年，虜遣安平公涉歸幡能健……東擊青州。

translations.literal: Commentary: According to the Barbarian Wei Account: "In the first year of Jingping, the barbarians sent the Anping Duke Shegui Fan Nengjian to attack Qing Province in the east."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: According to the Account of the Barbarian Wei: "In the first year of Jingping, the northerners sent the Duke of Anping, Shegui Fan Nengjian to strike east against Qing Province."

sentences.zh: 」涉歸幡能健即叔孫建，魏書有傳，魏道武時，曾賜爵安平公。

translations.literal: " Shegui Fan Nengjian is Shusun Jian; the Wei History has his biography; in the time of Emperor Daowu of Wei he was once granted the title Duke of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: " Shegui Fan Nengjian is Shusun Jian, who has a biography in the Wei History; under Emperor Daowu of Wei he had once been enfeoffed as Duke of Anping.

sentences.zh: 庚辰 張熷讀史舉正云：「二月丁丑、庚辰書辛未前，誤。

translations.literal: Gengchen. Zhang Huang's Corrections in Reading History says: "To place the second month's dingchou and gengchen before xinwei is an error.
translations.idiomatic: Gengchen. Zhang Huang's Corrections in Reading History says: "Placing the second month's dingchou and gengchen before xinwei is an error.

sentences.zh: 」按張說是。

translations.literal: " Commentary: Zhang is correct.
translations.idiomatic: " Commentary: Zhang is correct.

sentences.zh: 二月戊辰朔，初四日辛未，初十日丁丑，十三日庚辰，辛未不當在庚辰後。

translations.literal: The second month began on wuchen; the fourth day was xinwei, the tenth day dingchou, the thirteenth day gengchen; xinwei ought not to come after gengchen.
translations.idiomatic: The second month began on wuchen; the fourth day was xinwei, the tenth dingchou, the thirteenth gengchen—xinwei should not appear after gengchen.

sentences.zh: 爵蒙遜為驃騎大將軍 各本皆無「驃騎」二字。

translations.literal: Mengxun was ennobled as Grand General of Agile Cavalry: in all editions the two characters "Agile Cavalry" are missing.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun ennobled Grand General of Agile Cavalry: all editions omit the words "Agile Cavalry."

sentences.zh: 按本書文帝紀，元嘉二年，驃騎大將軍涼州牧大沮渠蒙遜改為車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Commentary: According to this book's Annals of Emperor Wen, in the second year of Yuanjia the Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Liang Province, the Great Juqu Mengxun, was changed to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: According to the Annals of Emperor Wen in this book, in the second year of Yuanjia the Grand General of Agile Cavalry and governor of Liang Province, the Great Juqu Mengxun, was changed to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 則各本並奪「驃騎」二字。

translations.literal: Thus all editions alike have dropped the two characters "Agile Cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: Thus all editions alike have dropped the words "Agile Cavalry."

sentences.zh: 今據南史補。

translations.literal: Now supplemented according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The words are now restored from the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 富陽人孫法光反 「孫法光」，褚叔度傳作「孫法亮」。

translations.literal: Sun Faguang of Fuyang rebelled: "Sun Faguang" in the biography of Chu Shudu is written "Sun Faliang."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Faguang of Fuyang rebelled: the biography of Chu Shudu has "Sun Faliang" instead of "Sun Faguang."

sentences.zh: 會稽太守褚淡之遣山陰令陸劭討敗之 「褚淡之」各本並作「褚談」，據褚叔度傳，時會稽太守為褚淡之，「談」蓋「淡」之形譌。

translations.literal: Chuji Commandery Administrator Chu Danzhi sent Shanyin Magistrate Lu Shao to attack and defeat him: "Chu Danzhi" in all editions is written "Chu Tan"; according to the biography of Chu Shudu, the administrator of Kuaiji at the time was Chu Danzhi; "Tan" is presumably a graphic corruption of "Dan."
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji administrator Chu Danzhi sent Shanyin magistrate Lu Shao to defeat him: all editions read "Chu Tan" for "Chu Danzhi"; according to the biography of Chu Shudu the administrator of Kuaiji at the time was Chu Danzhi, and "Tan" is presumably a graphic corruption of "Dan."

sentences.zh: 按南北朝人名後之「之」字，有時可以省去。

translations.literal: Commentary: The character zhi after personal names in the Northern and Southern Dynasties can sometimes be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In Northern and Southern Dynasties personal names, the final character zhi is sometimes omitted.

sentences.zh: 今仍改「談」作「淡」，並補「之」字。

translations.literal: Now "Tan" is still changed to "Dan," and the character zhi is supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: The text now changes "Tan" to "Dan" and restores the character zhi.

sentences.zh: 殺虜潁川太守庾龍 「潁川」各本並作「潁州」，據劉粹傳改。

translations.literal: Killed the barbarian Administrator of Yingchuan, Yu Long: "Yingchuan" in all editions is written "Ying Province"; changed according to the biography of Liu Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Killed the enemy administrator of Yingchuan, Yu Long: all editions read "Ying Province" for "Yingchuan"; changed according to the biography of Liu Cui.

sentences.zh: 以旱詔赦五歲刑以下罪人 各本並脫「刑」字，據南史補。

translations.literal: Because of drought, an edict pardoned offenders below five years' punishment: in all editions the character "punishment" is dropped; supplemented according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Drought amnesty for those below five years' punishment: all editions drop the word "punishment"; restored from the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙寅 按景平元年十二月癸巳朔，無丙寅。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, bingyin. Commentary: In the twelfth month of the first year of Jingping new moon falls on guisi; there is no bingyin.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, bingyin. Commentary: In the twelfth month of Jingping year one the new moon was guisi; there is no bingyin.

sentences.zh: 二年春二月癸巳朔日有蝕之 「二月癸巳朔」，局本同，宋本、北監本、毛本、殿本、通鑑考異引宋略、建康實錄作「正月癸巳朔」，南史宋本紀作「二月己卯朔」。

translations.literal: Second year, spring, second month, on guisi new moon there was a solar eclipse: "second month, guisi new moon"—the Bureau edition agrees; Song edition, Northern Directorate edition, Mao edition, Palace edition, and the Comprehensive Mirror's textual notes citing Song Summary and Veritable Records of Jiankang have "first month, guisi new moon"; the Annals of Song in the History of the Southern Dynasties has "second month, jimao new moon."
translations.idiomatic: Second year, spring, second month, solar eclipse on guisi new moon: for "second month, guisi new moon" the Bureau edition agrees, while the Song, Northern Directorate, Mao, and Palace editions and the Comprehensive Mirror's notes citing the Song Summary and Veritable Records of Jiankang read "first month, guisi new moon," and the Song annals in the History of the Southern Dynasties read "second month, jimao new moon."

sentences.zh: 按陳垣朔閏表，景平二年正月癸亥朔，二月壬辰朔。

translations.literal: Commentary: According to Chen Yuan's table of new and intercalary moons, in the second year of Jingping the first month began on guihai and the second month on renchen.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: According to Chen Yuan's table of new and intercalary moons, in Jingping year two the first month began on guihai and the second on renchen.

sentences.zh: 查正月無癸巳，癸巳為二月初二日。

translations.literal: Checking shows there is no guisi in the first month; guisi is the second day of the second month.
translations.idiomatic: The first month has no guisi; guisi is the second day of the second month.

sentences.zh: 然日蝕當在朔日，是年正月祇二十九日，作二月壬辰朔者，蓋後人定朔有誤。

translations.literal: Yet a solar eclipse ought to fall on the new-moon day; that year the first month had only twenty-nine days—those who make the second month begin on renchen presumably erred in later calendrical fixing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet an eclipse should fall on the new-moon day; that year the first month had only twenty-nine days, so making the second month begin on renchen is presumably a later calendrical error.

sentences.zh: 宋書五行志作「二月癸巳朔」。

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Five Phases in the Book of Song has "second month, guisi new moon."
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on the Five Phases in the Book of Song reads "second month, guisi new moon."

sentences.zh: 今改從局本。

translations.literal: Now changed to follow the Bureau edition.
translations.idiomatic: The text now follows the Bureau edition.

sentences.zh: 乙未以皇弟義恭為冠軍將軍南豫州刺史乙巳大風 按陳垣朔閏表景平二年正月癸亥朔，是月無乙未、乙巳。

translations.literal: On yiwei the emperor's younger brother Yigong was made General Who Vanquishes the Enemy and Inspector of South Yu Province; on yisi a great wind blew. Commentary: According to Chen Yuan's table, in the second year of Jingping the first month began on guihai; that month has no yiwei or yisi.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Prince Yigong was made General Who Vanquishes the Enemy and inspector of South Yu Province; on yisi a great wind blew. Commentary: Chen Yuan's table gives Jingping year two, first month, new moon guihai—that month has no yiwei or yisi.

sentences.zh: 二月壬辰朔，初三日乙未，十三日乙巳。

translations.literal: The second month began on renchen; the third day was yiwei, the thirteenth day yisi.
translations.idiomatic: The second month began on renchen; the third day was yiwei and the thirteenth yisi.

sentences.zh: 可證上之春正月應作春二月。

translations.literal: This proves that the "spring, first month" above should read "spring, second month."
translations.idiomatic: This shows that "spring, first month" above should read "spring, second month."

sentences.zh: 江州刺史王弘南兗州刺史檀道濟入朝 各本並作「江州刺史檀道濟、揚州刺史王弘入朝」。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiang Province Wang Hong and Inspector of South Yan Province Tan Daoji entered court: in all editions it is written "Inspector of Jiang Province Tan Daoji and Inspector of Yang Province Wang Hong entered court."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, inspector of Jiang Province, and Tan Daoji, inspector of South Yan Province, came to court: all editions read "Tan Daoji, inspector of Jiang Province, and Wang Hong, inspector of Yang Province."

sentences.zh: 建康實錄作「江州刺史王弘、南兗州刺史檀道濟來朝」，是，今據改。

translations.literal: The Veritable Records of Jiankang has "Inspector of Jiang Province Wang Hong and Inspector of South Yan Province Tan Daoji came to court"—correct; now changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records of Jiankang has "Wang Hong, inspector of Jiang Province, and Tan Daoji, inspector of South Yan Province, came to court"—which is correct, and the text is now changed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 錢大昕廿二史考異云：「按是時道濟為南兗州刺史，非江州；

translations.literal: Qian Daxin's Collected Variants in the Twenty-two Histories says: "Commentary: At this time Daoji was Inspector of South Yan Province, not Jiang;
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daxin's Collected Variants in the Twenty-two Histories says: "Commentary: At this time Daoji was inspector of South Yan Province, not Jiang;

sentences.zh: 弘為江州刺史，非揚州也。

translations.literal: Hong was Inspector of Jiang Province, not Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was inspector of Jiang Province, not Yang.

sentences.zh: 揚州治輦下，時以司空徐羨之領之。

translations.literal: Yang Province administered the capital region; at the time Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi held it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Province administered the capital; at the time Xu Xianzhi as Minister of Works held it concurrently.

sentences.zh: 紀所書皆誤。」

translations.literal: What the annal records is all in error."
translations.idiomatic: What the annal records is all wrong."

sentences.zh: 西將軍宜都王

translations.literal: General Who Guards the West, Prince of Yidu
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the West, Prince of Yidu

translations.literal: 〈to this point〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈to this point〉

sentences.zh: 撫心摧塞 各本並脫，今據元龜一八八補。

translations.literal: Presses her heart and is crushed: in all editions this is missing; now supplemented according to the Yuanjian, section 188.
translations.idiomatic: "Presses her heart and is utterly crushed": all editions omit this; it is now restored from the Yuanjian, section 188.

sentences.zh: 始徐羨之傅亮將廢帝

translations.literal: At first Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang were about to depose the emperor
translations.idiomatic: At first Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang were about to depose the emperor

translations.literal: 〈to this point〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈to this point〉

sentences.zh: 時年十九 此段宋本巳有脫葉。

translations.literal: He was nineteen years old. Commentary: This passage in the Song edition already had lacunae.
translations.idiomatic: He was nineteen years old. Commentary: This passage was already defective in the Song edition.

sentences.zh: 北監本、毛本、殿本、局本據南史補。

translations.literal: The Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions supplemented it according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions restored it from the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 今仍錄存。

translations.literal: It is still recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: It is still recorded here.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之、傅亮、檀道濟、謝晦等入雲龍門至華林園廢少帝一段，又見沈約宋書徐羨之傳中。

translations.literal: The passage in which Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, Tan Daoji, Xie Hui, and others entered Cloud Dragon Gate and reached Hualin Park to depose Emperor Shao is also found in Shen Yue's Book of Song, biography of Xu Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The account of Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, Tan Daoji, Xie Hui, and others entering Cloud Dragon Gate and reaching Hualin Park to depose Emperor Shao also appears in Shen Yue's Book of Song, biography of Xu Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 天淵池，各本作天泉池，蓋據李延壽南史，乃避唐諱。

translations.literal: Heavenly Abyss Pool: in all editions it is written Heavenly Spring Pool, presumably following Li Yanshou's History of the Southern Dynasties, avoiding Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly Abyss Pool: all editions read Heavenly Spring Pool, presumably following Li Yanshou's History of the Southern Dynasties to avoid Tang taboo.

sentences.zh: 今仍據沈約宋書徐羨之傳改為天淵池。

translations.literal: Now it is still changed back to Heavenly Abyss Pool according to Shen Yue's Book of Song, biography of Xu Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The name is now restored to Heavenly Abyss Pool from Shen Yue's Book of Song, biography of Xu Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 其難乎哉 各本並脫此一行，僅涵芬樓影印百衲本所據之宋本，有此殘葉。

translations.literal: How hard it is! In all editions this line is missing; only the Song edition underlying the Hanfenlou photolithograph of the Hundred-Block edition has this surviving leaf.
translations.idiomatic: "How hard it is!" All editions omit this line; only the Song edition underlying the Hanfenlou photolithograph of the Hundred-Block edition preserves this surviving leaf.

sentences.zh: 蓋即本卷史臣曰之殘存結尾語。

translations.literal: Presumably it is the surviving closing words of this scroll's historian's appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: It is presumably the surviving closing line of this scroll's historian's appraisal.
